outcome: For one exact encrypted knowledge-material object, establish verified protection across an operational SQL layer, an independently failed recovery-journal layer, and an immutable SQL-independent archive layer; then reconstruct and verify the object into any conforming SQL realization without confusing copy, replay, import, or database startup with restoration proof.
scope: SQL-portable three-layer protection and verified restoration for immutable encrypted artifact and recipient-envelope bytes, with PostgreSQL as the first adapter and Docker as a local conformance environment.
exclusions: treating three copies inside one effective failure domain as three-layer protection
making PostgreSQL, SQL dialect, container, volume, provider, or locator identity part of immutable object identity
using PostgreSQL WAL, physical database pages, or vendor dumps as the portable recovery authority
claiming backup completion without exact object identity closure across all required layers
claiming restoration from copy, replay, import, process start, or query success without destination retrieval and verification
storing plaintext, unwrapped content keys, private keys, or credentials
selecting production topology, region, credentials, retention, RPO, RTO, publication, release, or deployment

revision_history.change: Authored SQL-portable three-layer protection and verified recovery successor capability.

challenge_route: Challenge product meaning through the Knowledge Exchange Protocol product owner, SQL portability through the Durable Storage capability owner, and adapter or recovery evidence through their exact implementation and conformance owners.
claim_limit: Authored successor Product Capability candidate only; no adoption, ontology admission, implementation conformance, production provider, publication, deployment, or external effect.
